newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST -Nat Power profits to dip, div up.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST -Nat Power profits to dip, div up.

text.p: British electricity generator National Power Plc should see a slight decline in first half pretax profits when it reports on November 20 but it should raise its dividend and may signal further growth, analysts said.
"Strong, ordinary dividend growth will be the order of the day," said one sector analyst who asked not to be named.
National Power is forecast show pretax profits of between 210 and 253 million stg, down from 254 million stg, and pay a dividend of 5.94 to 6.5 pence against 5.4 pence previously.
The company said in July that first-half profits could be lower than last year, citing a shorter reporting period and the seasonal nature of its business.
Analysts said indications were that the company might offer 10-12 percent dividend growth in the future.
"There are unlikely to be any great surprises. The company has done quite a lot to educate the market," the analyst said.
National Power said in September that the net effect on profit after tax of income from international investments should be around 30 million stg in 1996/97, rising to 95 million stg a year later.

Analysts said that for the first half, the impact on pretax profits was likely to be negligible but they added that the figures reflected the company's strategy of moving towards overseas investments.
"Given the constraints National Power faces in the UK, it makes sense for them to focus overseas," said the analyst.
National Power was stymied in its plans to acquire a regional electricity company (Rec) when its 2.5 billion stg bid for Southern Electric was blocked by the UK government in April.
It also sold off 4,000 megaWatts of coal-fired generating plant to Hanson Plc's Eastern Group in order to fulfil undertakings on competition given to industry watchdog Offer.
It now has some 900 million stg of international investments, the analyst said, "and their contribution is now kicking in".
But analysts said the UK electricity market was looking more buoyant than anticipated, which could help volumes for National Power even if prices were not strongly affected.
National Power's cousin PowerGen said demand was up three percent when it reported a four percent rise in first-half pretax profits to 138 million stg on November 14.
"Three percent is very, very strong and that certainly helps the generators," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
"It will be interesting to see how hard National Power fights to keep its market share in the UK," the analyst said.
